VALIDATOR FINDINGS DURING THE BUILD (fixed before the final run): the designer's mockup was never validated and two constructs were INVALID: s-text-field has no inputMode prop and no onKeyDown prop (calculator.html used inputMode). Fallbacks: inputMode dropped (no numeric-keypad hint on mobile; s-number-field was rejected for the revenue field because it sanitises non-numeric text before the validator can name the problem); Enter-to-calculate moved to a wrapper <div onKeyDown> that receives the composed keydown from the field (re-verified in Chromium: enter_key_calculates=true). Newly confirmed VALID (previously unverified in DESIGN-NOTES-v2 section 8): s-query-container, s-grid, s-box, s-stack, s-switch, s-heading, s-paragraph, s-text, s-divider, s-table, s-table-header-row, s-table-header, s-table-body, s-table-row, s-table-cell.

app/routes/app.tsx (the s-app-nav change) was submitted to validate_component_codeblocks and the validator returned INVALID: 's-app-nav' is an App Bridge web component (not in the polaris-app-home type universe) and the Polaris Link type has no 'rel' prop. Same namespace limitation pass 1 and pass 2 documented, not a defect in the markup, so app.tsx is deliberately NOT listed as a validation (an INVALID entry would poison overall_status); its raw INVALID output is kept in records/mcp-raw-validator-output.json (result 8). The nav is covered by tests/ui/app-nav.test.ts and the shopify.dev docs (rel=home is hidden from the menu).

app/components/expense-breakdown.tsx contains inline <svg> (the ADR-0004 hand-rolled donut), which the validator does not inspect (listed under 'Non-Shopify components (not validated)'); its markup was checked by tests, axe and Chromium instead.

axe-core 4.10.2 (tools/harness/axe.mjs; results in axe-results.json) reports ONE critical rule on every page containing an s-table: aria-required-children on Polaris's own shadow-DOM <div role=grid> ('Required ARIA children role not present: rowgroup, row'). I judge this an axe false positive: the s-table-row/-cell hosts get their roles through ElementInternals, which axe cannot read, and Chromium's real accessibility tree (chromium-ax-tree-results-table.txt) shows grid > row(columnheader x4) + rowgroup > row(gridcell ...). The designer's documented fallback (native table + caption) was therefore NOT applied. NOT verified: a screen-reader pass; that judgement is mine, not an authority's. Measured and related: the grid has NO accessible name (a host aria-label is not exposed, and axe flagged it aria-prohibited-attr), so the aria-label was removed and the table is introduced only by its section heading. At narrow widths Polaris renders s-table as a plain list without table semantics (by design; not checked below 560px). Other axe findings: 'region' on s-app-nav (harness only: outside the Admin the nav renders inline); 'document-title' was REAL (root.tsx had no <title>) and is fixed; color-contrast came back 'incomplete' (needs review), not measured.

BROWSER RENDER (Chromium, hydrated harness: the real route modules server-rendered and hydrated, the real polaris.js (downloaded from the CDN, served from disk; sha256 in SUMMARY-4.1.md), stubbed authenticate/shop-context and in-memory repositories only - the REAL services run). Screenshots at 1000px and 600px for every page and state, before (commit 91d74ed) and after, are in screenshots/. Polaris s-page hoists its header (title, breadcrumbs, primary and secondary actions) OUT of the iframe when window.shopify exists (polaris.js: isEmbedded = window.shopify defined), so screenshots are taken with window.shopify undefined (header rendered by Polaris) and the interaction runs (window.shopify stubbed to record toasts) have no header. NOT SEEN (needs the live Admin iframe): the App Bridge sidebar nav, the contextual save bar (dirty detection on hidden inputs plus dotted-name s-* controls, Save/Discard, the Leave-page prompt), the real toast, and every HEADER ACTION (Calculate, Save calculation, Edit rules, Reset to placeholder defaults, Change revenue, New calculation, Duplicate as new calculation): in the Admin these buttons are drawn by the Admin chrome, so whether their onClick / commandFor='--show' (opening the save/reset modal) reach the iframe elements is unverified.

live_store_items: Sidebar (Admin): the app entry 'Expense Calculator' lists exactly two children, 'Expense rules' and 'History' (no 'Calculator' child); the app name opens /app/calculator; 'Expense rules' highlights on /app/rules; History highlights on /app/history and /app/history/:id.

Header actions in the Admin title bar work: Calculator -> Calculate (validates, then goes to Results) and Edit rules; Rules -> Reset to placeholder defaults (opens the confirm modal; 'Replace values' fills the form); Results -> Save calculation (opens the save modal; Save creates the snapshot and lands on History detail with the 'Calculation saved' toast) and Change revenue; History -> New calculation; History detail -> Duplicate as new calculation.

Rules page save bar: editing any switch / rule type / value shows the App Bridge save bar; Discard restores the saved values and clears any error banner; Save persists and shows the 'Rule changes saved' toast with a Calculate action that opens the Calculator; 'Reset to placeholder defaults' makes the save bar appear (a synthetic input/change event is dispatched on the form) and Discard undoes it; navigating away with unsaved edits raises the Leave-page prompt.

After saving rules, the Calculator's read-only summary shows the saved values and Calculate/Results use them (e.g. Shipping 777.25 appears in the Results row and total); a saved-OFF category is absent from Results.

Calculator: the currency select shows 'USD - US Dollar' immediately on first open and after Change revenue / Duplicate (no blank flash); typing -5, 1,5, 10.555, 1e5 shows the exact message live; Enter in the revenue field calculates.

Results: metric tiles are three columns at a normal Admin width; the breakdown table and donut sit side by side; the header shows the breadcrumb 'Calculator'. History detail: the header shows the breadcrumb 'History' and the Duplicate action; the snapshot banner, lock badge and engine version are visible.
